newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF says decision on Russia loan maybe next week.
newsitem.headline: IMF says decision on Russia loan maybe next week.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund could decide by the end of next week whether to release delayed payments of a $10 billion three-year loan to Russia, chief representative Thomas Wolf said on Tuesday.

But Wolf said the IMF's next regular monitoring mission would probably not arrive in the Russian capital until the week after that. "The assessment is under way now and will probably be completed by early next week," he said.
"If it is positive then there would likely be a board meeting around mid-month and right after that the regular monitoring mission would arrive."
The IMF board takes a final decision on whether to pay tranches of loans given to member countries.

The IMF delayed paying tranches of the loan in October and in November because it was worried about low tax collection. IMF officials said they were looking for evidence of a sustainable improvement in revenue collection before releasing the money.
Russian officials have since stressed that revenue collection has improved and they have set up a special emergency committee to force tax debtors to pay.

A handful of companies, including carmaker Avtovaz, face the threat of bankruptcy proceedings and ministers say they will hold managers personally responsible if companies do not pay their taxes on time.

Interfax news agency on Tuesday quoted Finance Minister Alexander Livshits as saying that the current three-year loan would be Russia's last credit from the IMF because Russia would be cooperating with the international community in a different way by the time the loan expired.
Russia tapped international financial markets last month, raising $1 billion in its first sovereign eurobond since the 1917 Bolshevik revolution brought the communists to power.
